reason: I'd install the portable zip because waiting for Bridge or Photoshop just to look at a file is a real daily annoyance and it costs me nothing. But my catalogue, XMP and colour setup can't break, and a 0.4.1 from one person hasn't earned the right to be my default yet.
why_switch_or_not: The fast open and next/back numbers and the RAW/PSD/EXR support are exactly what I want for quick looks, so I'd try it and maybe point JPG/PNG/WebP at it. I wouldn't hand over RAW or PSD double-click, because nothing here says it reads or respects XMP or Lightroom/Bridge ratings and metadata, and its own sidecar edit file is one more thing that could clash with my pipeline. The ICC support sounds good, but I'd need to compare it against Photoshop on my own wide-gamut files before I trusted it.
current_app_pros: Bridge, Lightroom and Photoshop hold my catalogue, XMP sidecars, ratings and keywords, and the colour handling is the reference everything else is judged against. Plugins and presets all live there, and nothing surprises me.
current_app_pains: Double-clicking a file in Explorer launches a heavy Adobe app, and I wait several seconds to see one picture. Flipping through a folder quickly is slow, and it all eats RAM and disk.
objection: One developer, version 0.4.1, no plug-in system, and no mention of XMP or catalogue awareness. If it mangles colour or my sidecars, it breaks a pipeline I can't afford to break.
would_change_my_mind: Proof that it reads XMP ratings and labels without writing to my files, and that its colour output matches Photoshop on my own ICC files. A few months of stable releases would help too.
